# ONE-DAY LICENSES

One day licenses may be purchased online or on site at the event. Below are the categories eligible for one-day licenses:

<visual_element id="e1">
**One-Day License Eligibility Flow**

**BEGINNER ONE-DAY** (dark navy blue box)  
→ **Eligibility** (dark navy blue box)  
- Road/Track/CX: Novice
- MTB: Novice/Cat. 2

**EXPERIENCED ONE-DAY** (red box)  
→ **Eligibility** (red box)  
- Road/Track/CX: Cat. 1-4
- MTB: Pro-Cat. 1

Both flows use gold right-pointing arrows connecting the license category boxes on the left to their corresponding eligibility boxes on the right.
</visual_element>

# MEMBER ACCOUNTS AND VERIFICATION

In recent years USA Cycling has moved towards electronic licenses, which includes an e-license on the USA Cycling app for iOS and Android. A rider’s account may also be verified through the USA Cycling website, which mirrors information on the app. Below are some considerations when assessing rider eligibility.

<visual_element id="e2">
**Member Accounts and Verification — Key Considerations**

Four dark navy blue oval callouts, arranged in alternating left-right positions:

1. **Upper left: Source of truth**

   A rider’s member account at usacycling.org serves as the “source of truth” for all aspects of a member’s license.

2. **Upper right: BikeReg registration and validation**

   Riders who register through BikeReg have their information validated upon entry. Note that a rider’s status (ie. category) may change between entry and the event.

3. **Lower left: Account changes and app updates**

   Changes to a member’s USA Cycling account appear in the USAC app immediately. In some cases a rider may need to log out and log back in to refresh the information.

4. **Lower right: Weekly database download**

   A weekly database download of current member license information is available for event organizers to assist with registration.

Gravel Burn introduces 'new dimension' of teams classification at October stage race while schedules revealed for BWR and Grasshopper series - Gravel Bits
Date: Tue Oct 13 20:01:38 2026 UTC

The second edition of the seven-day Gravel Burn gravel stage race in South Africa, October 25-31, introduces a teams classification with points to determine standings and prizes. It will be the first such classification recognition at a gravel stage race.
Trade teams of three to four riders, as well as alliances of independent riders, will be eligible for the new classification. The top three riders from each team will earn points that will contribute to the daily standings. 
Organisers developed the format in collaboration with several individuals, including pro road and gravel veteran Peter Stetina of Canyon x DT Swiss ATR and Adam Hansen, president of the CPA (Cyclistes Professionnels Associés), both having participated in last year's inaugural race.
"This innovation provides another dimension to the racing and also rewards the riders' efforts and the teams' investment," said race founder Kevin Vermaak. 
"Independent 'privateer' racers formed the foundation of professional gravel racing, adding to the 'freedom' and charm of gravel. We recognise that the emergence of 'superteams' is a threat to that. That's why we opened the Teams Classification to all to help level the playing field, where they may form ad-hoc teams to compete with the more formal outfits."
Canyon x DT Swiss ATR will field a women's team led by former Unbound Gravel 200 winner Carolin Schiff. They will also start two men's teams, one led by former US gravel champion Bradyn Lange. Scott-SRAM will have one team in each division, the women's team including Life Time Grand Prix contender Alexis Skarda and the men's team with Filippo Colombo, who won the UCI Gravel World Series Ceder race in February. Toyota Specialized Imbuko will have two men's teams with all-South African rosters, while Mattia De Marchi will lead a three-rider men's team for The Grip.
The solo race remains the foundation of Nedbank Gravel Burn, with a $150,000 US prize purse split equally between the pro women and pro men categories, including daily payouts to the top 3 and overall top 10. Gravel Burn is a full-service stage race in the Eastern Cape of South Africa, covering 750 kilometres and 8,500 metres of elevation gain.
Among the debutants for individuals are two-time Marathon MTB world champion Henrique Avancini of Brazil, multi-time Japanese XCO mountain bike champion Kohei Yamamoto, as well as 18-year road pro and a former Cape Epic winner Jakob Fuglsang.
Last year's men's champion Matt Beers returns, as well as runner-up Simon Pellaud. Women's champion Axelle Dubau-Prevot will defend her title, lining up against third-placed Hayley Preen.

Belgian Waffle Ride series seeks sixth event in Colorado

[Image 0: Cecile Lejeune (Trek Driftless) on her way to a solo victory at Belgian Waffle Ride Utah]
Five events have been confirmed for the Belgian Waffle Ride schedule next year, with a new Colorado event taking shape. Registration opened October 13 for a quartet of US events spread from March to September, while Mexico takes place in late November. 
A usual suspect in the series has been Utah, but it may be a standalone race in 2027, according to organisers, and could become a UCI Gravel World Series qualifier.
The Quad-Tripel Crown was won this year by Hayden Christian (Trek-MAAP Pro.Fwd) and Cécile Lejeune (Trek Driftless).

30th season for Grasshopper Adventure Series

[Image 1: Jen Tavé won the final two Hoppers and won the women's overall at the 2025 Grasshopper Adventure Series]
The race schedule for the 2027 Grasshopper Adventure Series, now in its 30th year, was released with five races in northern California. The opener takes place at Low Gap on January 31, a 59-mile gravel event with 95% dirt tracks in Ukiah, and culminates at Ukiah Mendo Epic on May 23, a 70-mile mixed-terrain adventure in the same area. 
The middle of the schedule includes the classic mixed-terrain Huffmaster on February 28, the road and climbing-heavy King Ridge on March 20 and the gravel-singletrack challenge of Jackson Forest on April 10.
Registration is open, and a series pass for all five events is $675, plus fees, with individual races at $155 each. Prices go up after November 30, two months before the opener.
Last year, Jen Tavé (SpeedBlock-Terún Pro Cycling) and Cassius Anderson (Marin Service Course) secured the overall titles for elite divisions in the five-race Grasshopper Series.

L27: ## INSTRUCTIONAL GUIDE
L28: 
L29: The LiveReg app integrates your event day registration with your existing athleteReg event, letting you process credit cards on site and keep all your data in one place. At its simplest, LiveReg acts as a basic point-of-sale system; at its most complex, it can be a fully-featured paperless registration system.
L30: 
L31: ## TABLE OF CONTENTS
L32:

L35:   * 【5†Getting Started】

L37:   * 【7†Troubleshooting & Support】
L38: ## MENU KEY
L39:

L41:

L44:   * Set event day surcharge

L48: 
L49:   * View all entries (including pre-registration entries in your account, pending entries, and approved day-of entries)
L50:   * For each entry: accept payment, assign bibs, print release forms, edit, or delete
L51:   * Search for participants
L52:

L67: ## USAGE MODES
L68: Depending on your event setup and waivers required, choose one of these three modes of use:
L69: Simple: Point of Sale (Payment Only, No Registration Data)
L70: Run your registration with paper forms as normal, but process credit cards and have the funds deposited into your athleteReg event director account.
L71: Workflow Sign into LiveReg, select your event, and use the "Point of Sale" option to process credit cards as needed.
L72: Moderate: Data Entry (Payment Processing & Paper Registration Data)
L73: Run your registration with paper forms as normal, process credit cards to add funds, and manually add participant registration data to your athleteReg account. This gives you an electronic record of all your day-of participants in your event director account, which you can use for post-event emails, sending start lists, or any other data tracking you may need.
L74: Workflow Set up your registration area as normal with paper forms and pens for day-of participants. When a participant brings their form to the registration table, enter that participant’s information into the LiveReg App as a manual entry (for USAC-sanctioned events in BikeReg, use the USAC License # lookup to quickly fill out all the fields). Take payment for the entry and assign the participant a bib number.
L75: To email a final start list to your timer, go to your "Events" menu item and choose "Email Start List".
L76: Complex: Kiosk or Mobile Device Signup (Payment Processing & Paperless Registration)
L77: Participants register for the event electronically, using kiosks you’ve placed in the registration area or their mobile device. After registering, they come to the registration table to pay and receive a bib number.
L78: Workflow Post the event day registration url in the registration area and/or provide your own kiosks – a computer or tablet device with a browser pointed to the event day registration url. Participants sign up on their phone or a kiosk and then go to the registration table.
L79: If you need a "wet signature," you can print a prefilled release form using their registration information directly from LiveReg; all they have to do is sign. If your event has an electronic waiver, they agree to it during the registration process.
L80: At the registration table, assign their entry a bib number and collect payment.
L81: To email a final start list to your timer, go to your "Events" menu item and choose "Email Start List".
L82: ## GETTING STARTED
L83: 
L84: To get started with LiveReg, sign in to your event director account on the appropriate athleteReg site:
L85: 【14†Image】
L86: 
L87: Next, select the event you will be doing day-of registration for and move the "Open Registration" slider to the right. This turns on "event day" mode for that event, which will allow participants with the right url to register on their phone. It will also allow you to process credit cards and add entries for that event.
L88: 【15†Image】
L89: Enter the event day surcharge (how much more it costs to enter the event on-site than it did for pre-registration) and how long you want to keep event day registration open for. You will be able to override any surcharges later if necessary.
L90: 【16†Image】
L91: Once registration is open, you’ll see a URL for event-day registration for your event. If you want to allow participants to enter via their phones, you can distribute this URL to them at the venue. The URL will be the same for your event every time you open registration, so you can turn it on a few days prior to check the URL if you’d like.
L92: 【17†Image】
L93: ## PROCESSING TRANSACTIONS
L94: To get started with LiveReg, sign in to your event director account on the appropriate athleteReg site:
L95: Quick Sale
L96: applies to: all modes
L97: If all you want to do is collect money from credit cards, you can use the quick sale button on the left to open up a form for swiping credit cards, and optionally entering notes (i.e. "payment for extra race shirt") and/or emailing a receipt for the transaction. This does not add the entry to your start list. Funds are added to your athleteReg event director balance and data on the transaction is added as a merchandise item should you need to reference it later.
L98: You can also select the payment type to be cash/check if you simply need to account for a transaction without running a credit card.
L99: 【18†Image】
L100: Manual Entries
L101: applies to: Data Entry and Device/Kiosk modes
L102: You can also enter racers into the LiveReg system from the app by touching the "Add" button.
L103: 【19†Image】 This prompts you to select a category and/or merchandise item for that participant. You may then supply as much or as little participant data as you want. To save time, you can also look up participant data by USAC # (for BikeReg events). This searches past BikeReg registrations with that USAC # and pulls in the most recent registration for that person.
L104: 【20†Image】
L105: Once you touch "Done" on this screen, the entry is added to the pending queue just like a kiosk entry and you can now take payment for it, assign a bib number, or print a release form from the "Entries" screen.
L106: Entries will be pending until a form of payment is confirmed (Credit Card/Cash/Check/Free).
L107: Event Day Registrations
L108: applies to: Kiosk mode
L109: Participants can use their mobile devices or a kiosk to register for the event at the event-day url, but payment is not collected until the participant comes to the registration table. A list of entries that have been entered online but not yet paid for is shown on the "Entries" screen:
L110: 【21†Image】
L111: When a participant comes to the registration table, find their name in the list by scrolling or using the search bar and touching "Payment."
L112: 【22†Image】
L113: This brings you to their entry, where you can edit it, assign a bib number, print a release form, and take payment. Select the payment method the participant is using and swipe the card or accept the cash/check.
L114: The payment amount will default to the entry fee for the category plus the event day surcharge, but you are free to edit it for whatever reason.
L115: Once you confirm payment, the entry becomes "approved" and the participant is now entered into the event. You will probably want to give them a bib number at this point, and record that number by touching the "Bib" button.
L116: 【23†Image】
L117: If you are using one of our pre-filled release forms (BikeReg only), you can also print that for the participant to sign. You’ll need to be on a wireless network with a compatible AirPrint printer.
L118: More on printer setup can be found at the end of this document.
L119: Processing Multiple Entries at a Time
L120: applies to: Kiosk mode
L121: A common scenario is one person paying for multiple registrations at once. Instead of taking separate payments for each pending entry, you can group the entries together and pay for them all at once.
L122: 【24†Image】
L123: 【25†Image】
L124: When this selector is turned on, you can add entries to the group by touching their row, and when you process a payment it will approve all the entries at once.
L125: Viewing all event entries
L126: applies to: Date Entry and Kiosk mode
L127: If you need to edit or view preregistered entries (e.g. moving a preregistered racer to a different category), turn off the "Event Day Only" slider on the pending entries queue. You can then search and edit all registrations for the event, not just the event day ones.
L128: 【26†Image】
L129: Emailing a start list
L130: applies to: Date Entry and Device/Kiosk mode
L131: When registration for a category closes, you may want to send a final start list for the race to a timing service or the announcer. Touch the "Email Start List" button on the Events list to enter an email address to send the start list to. You can send specific category start data or all start data.
L132: 【27†Image】
L133: Release Forms and Printers applies to: Device/Kiosk mode
L134: If your event uses an online waiver, you can run a paperless event-day registration system by having all participants register for the event on their phone or at a kiosk you’ve set up. As part of the registration process, they’ll agree to the online waiver just like any pre-registrant did.
L135: However, if you need a wet signature on a paper waiver for each participant and you are using one of our standard waivers (BikeReg), you can print prefilled waivers directly from the app. LiveReg supports Apple’s AirPrint system, so all you need is an AirPrint-enabled printer on the same wireless network as your LiveReg app for this to work.
L136: Information on setting up AirPrint can be found here: 【28†https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201387†support.apple.com】
L137: By clicking on the settings icon on the left you can choose which release form you want to use. This will be remembered so that all entries are printed with the same form.
L138: When you’re taking payment for an entry or a group of entries, you can print the release form(s) via the "Release" or "Print All Release Forms" button. This prompts you to select which printer to send it to.
L139: 【29†Image】
L140: ## TROUBLESHOOTING & SUPPORT
L141: We do not offer full support on weekends, so please be sure to test out all functionality you plan to use before event day. Contact us ahead of time with questions Monday – Friday between 8:30 am and 8:30 pm ET: (888) 956-9560 or 【30†[email protected]】.
L142: For other issues, please see the list below and refer to the rest of the guide.
L143: Connectivity
L144: You need a stable wifi connection to use LiveReg. Check that you will have adequate service at your event location beforehand.
L145: More Features
L146: Not finding the features you need? Open a web browser and sign in to your event director area to access your full suite of tools. Please do contact us with feedback – 【31†[email protected]】.
L147: Swiper
L148: If swiper is not working, check connection of swiper to iPad. Credit card numbers can also be entered manually as needed.
L149: Modifying Start Lists
L150: Not able to send the download / start list format that your timing service or staff needs? Open a web browser and sign in to your event director area. Here you can create a new download template in the "Download Registration Data" area and save it. Go back to LiveReg and your download template will now be an option for emailing or printing your start list.
L151: Printing
L152: Need to print a start list? Email it to yourself, then open it in your preferred database program (i.e. Excel), format, and print. Or, open a web browser, access the "Download Registration Data" page in your event, download data, format, and print.
L153: If you are printing pre-filled release forms (BikeReg only), see the above section on AirPrint.

L17: # BikeReg and USA Cycling Launch First Round of New Offerings for Event Directors
L18: 
L19: The organizations have combined resources to improve the event registration process
L20: 
L21: (Easthampton, MA) July 16, 2019 – Since announcing their partnership in February of this year, BikeReg and USA Cycling have combined resources to launch three key offerings for directors of USA Cycling sanctioned events, and have also started work on the development of a roadmap for the future.
L22: The three offerings, which are now live, include Permit Integration, Online Waivers, and License Validation.
L23: 
L24: Online Waivers
L25: 
L26: BikeReg event directors can now use the USA Cycling online waiver, which also saves time for event directors. Using an API, BikeReg pulls the waiver connected to each registration directly from USA Cycling’s database. This keeps the BikeReg registration process quick and easy, while eliminating the need for participants to sign paper waivers.
L27: 
L28: 【7†Learn more about online waivers.】
L29: Permit Integration
L30: 
L31: Permit Integration was created as a way for event directors to save time when creating their events. Once they’ve completed the permit process with USA Cycling, they can use their permit number to autofill the event setup page on BikeReg.
L32: 
L33: 【8†Learn more about permit integration.】
L34: 
L35: License Validation
L36: Finally, BikeReg can now verify license numbers against USAC’s database, for all athletes registering on their site against category, date of birth, and gender. The process of checking the database happens in real time, so registering participants can renew, buy a license, and register right away.
L37: 
L38: 【9†Learn more about license validation.】
L39: 
L40: Improving a Proven Platform
L41: These offerings were designed to work seamlessly with BikeReg — the popular and proven registration and event management platform. Additional offerings, features, and tools will be developed over the next several months, with blogs, instructional guides, and other informative content being released as necessary. To stay tuned and up-to-date on the latest from BikeReg, sign up for the newsletter.
L42: 
L43: About BikeReg
L44: BikeReg is a single-source solution for online event registration and management. For event directors, the BikeReg system provides easy-to-use tools to design and customize the registration process for events. For participants, BikeReg helps track and register for events, set up notifications, view results and receipts, and more.
L45: BikeReg.com, a division of Pioneer Registration Services, LLC is based in Easthampton, Massachusetts. Find us at bikereg.com, contact us at (888) 956-9560 or Sales@BikeReg.com, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter (@bikereg).
L46: 
L47: About USA Cycling
L48: USA Cycling is a proud member of the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) and United States Olympic Committee (USOC). Within the United States, USA Cycling is the national governing body for the sport of cycling and oversees the disciplines of road, track, mountain bike, cyclocross, and BMX.
L49: With a mission to develop the sport of cycling in the United States and to achieve sustained international racing success, USA Cycling supports cyclists at all levels, from those just beginning in the sport and participating in fun rides to seasoned professionals.
L50: The organization not only identifies, develops, and selects cyclists to represent the United States in international competition, but also supports amateur bike racing through grassroots development programs and the provision of critical infrastructure to run organized racing.
L51: USA Cycling is headquartered in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and will celebrate its 100^{th} anniversary in 2020. In 1920, the organization began as The Amateur Bicycle League of America and evolved to become the United States Cycling Federation in 1975 and ultimately USA Cycling, Inc. in 1995. USA Cycling’s 100,000+ members are comprised of racers and cyclists of all ages and abilities, coaches, officials, mechanics, and race directors.
